public_notes.title: A Treaty-Era Record And Changing Woodlands
public_notes.text: The Band's account dates the reservation to an agreement finalized on September 30, 1854, at Lapointe on Madeline Island. That date concerns the reservation, not the origin of Ojibwe people. The same account describes its woodlands as pine lands clear-cut between 1850 and 1920. These passages place a treaty-era institution alongside a history of environmental change. They do not establish present boundaries or property title.

public_notes.title: Water Standards And Energy Resilience
public_notes.text: The Band's Water Resources page records adoption of Water Quality Standards on July 6, 2011, and describes a designated use for waters that support, or could support, wild rice habitat. Its Energy page links microgrid development to infrastructure outages during the 2016 flood and dates completed commissioning to May 2021. The shared thread is community-directed planning for water and essential services. These are attributed institutional accounts, not certification of current legal force, water safety, power output or service availability.
